summary: Separate pipeline responsibilities into source connection, datasource cleanup, reusable transforms, ontology-facing canonical outputs, and workflow/application consumption. Design backward from the operational ontology and use clear project boundaries for permissions, ownership, and maintainability.

attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Encode critical assumptions as machine-checkable preconditions and postconditions. Fail closed for invariant violations that would propagate bad data; use warnings only for genuinely non-blocking conditions. Validate key uniqueness, nullability, ranges, schema shape, and domain consistency before publication.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

summary: Production data engineering includes observability. Track build success, duration, freshness, ownership, upstream dependencies, and downstream consumers. Use lineage to estimate blast radius before changes and to trace downstream symptoms back to the actual upstream cause.

topic: batch incremental and streaming pipeline selection
attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Start with batch when it satisfies scale and latency because it is simpler to operate. Move to incremental processing when change volume makes full rebuilds inefficient, and choose streaming only when low-latency requirements justify the added complexity and slowest-component constraints.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Start operational application design from a shared domain model: objects for entities and events, properties for characteristics, links for relationships, and actions for governed changes. Keep UI logic downstream of this semantic layer so applications, analytics, and agents reuse the same definitions.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Choose the lowest-complexity application surface that satisfies the workflow. Prefer object-oriented or low-code builders for standard operational flows; use bounded custom widgets or functions for targeted extensions; move to a custom React or SDK application only when the experience or integration requirements require it.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

topic: application state widgets variables and events
attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Model UI state as typed dataflow. Widgets consume explicit inputs and emit explicit outputs; variables carry state; events coordinate selection, navigation, refresh, overlays, and action invocation. Prefer visible state transitions over hidden coupling so workflows remain testable and explainable.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

attribution: Palantir Learn + public Palantir Foundry docs (clean-room summary)
summary: Treat writes as typed governed actions rather than arbitrary UI-side mutations. Define parameters, validation, permissions, and success behavior around the domain model; let applications trigger those actions and react to confirmed completion. This improves integrity, auditability, and reuse across interfaces.
note: Clean-room synthesis; no verbatim certification-guide text.

topic: AIP bounded LLM tools and context
summary: Give an LLM only the ontology context, variables, functions, applications, searches, and actions required for its workflow. Describe each tool and state variable clearly, separate read from write access, and route ontology edits through defined actions instead of granting an unconstrained execution surface.

attribution: XUNIA clean-room synthesis from public Palantir engineering patterns
summary: For complex engineering missions, use a bounded specialist fleet: Intake/Source agent, Pipeline agent, Quality agent, Ontology agent, Application agent, Security agent, Release agent, and Observer agent. Give each role a narrow contract, run independent checks in parallel when dependencies allow, merge through explicit gates, require approval for consequential writes or releases, and preserve evidence for every claimed completion.

attribution: XUNIA clean-room synthesis from public Palantir engineering patterns
summary: Use the loop INSPECT -> MODEL -> PLAN -> DECOMPOSE -> EXECUTE -> VALIDATE -> OBSERVE -> REPAIR -> APPROVE -> RELEASE -> AUDIT. Ground plans in the ontology and data contracts, bound retries and tool permissions, prefer reversible changes, and do not promote a result until tests, data expectations, security checks, and downstream impact checks are satisfied.
